journeys.name: Governed release
journeys.actors: Builder and World owner through CLI or Connect
journeys.path: Candidate publication stores policy evidence; the owner activates one WorldRelease whose digest binds ontology, policy, executors, and components.
journeys.negativeProof: Same-World non-builder and missing policy both fail before any commit; stale activation fails.
journeys.replayProof: An identical candidate replay reauthorizes the current caller, returns the original publication, and creates no second commit; a revoked caller is denied.
journeys.isolationProof: Another World or Membership cannot publish or activate for this World; publication visibility grants no authority, and the digest remains bound to its World and four catalogs.
journeys.recoveryProof: A crash between publication and activation preserves the candidate and prior active pointer; retry converges to at most one active release.

completedBootstrapRecordBindings: policy evidence used by the ceremony

journeys.name: Governed knowledge
journeys.actors: Person asking Eve to remember a fact
journeys.path: Eve proposes and commits; one receipt and attributed evidence become queryable and explainable.
journeys.negativeProof: A normal member cannot write raw evidence; Eve does not claim memory before the receipt.
journeys.replayProof: The same operation returns the original receipt and creates no duplicate evidence or authority commit.
journeys.isolationProof: Another World or Membership cannot read the fact, evidence, receipt, or explanation.
journeys.recoveryProof: Committed evidence and its receipt survive Eve and projection restarts; a pending proposal resumes without claiming memory.

journeys.name: Shared authority
journeys.actors: Family member A proposing and family member B deciding
journeys.path: The decision uses B's principal; Commit creates one receipt, and the invite and Membership materialize atomically.
journeys.negativeProof: Self-approval outside policy, revoked Membership, and failed Commit create no partial Membership.
journeys.replayProof: Repeated Decide returns the original decision and deduplication result; repeated Commit returns the original CommitReceipt. Neither replay creates a second invite or Membership.
journeys.isolationProof: A principal from another World or family cannot decide the proposal or read the invite.
journeys.recoveryProof: A crash before Commit leaves no partial Membership; retry commits every artifact once, and a post-commit retry returns the original receipt.

journeys.name: Governed clinic query
journeys.path: Both read only permitted patient objects, page with sealed cursors, run server-budgeted compute, and explain the policy.
journeys.negativeProof: Cursor replay under another Membership or release fails; denied objects never affect public pagination, and the caller cannot raise the budget.
journeys.replayProof: The same sealed cursor and basis return the same authorized page and explanation; altered authority context is denied.
journeys.isolationProof: Denied patient objects affect no public values, counts, cursors, lineage, citations, or timing class.
journeys.recoveryProof: After restart, the server accepts a still-valid sealed cursor and basis or rejects it without widening the result.

journeys.name: Bound conversation
journeys.actors: Web A, WhatsApp through Kapso, Telegram A, and Telegram B
journeys.path: Every ingress resolves Account, Membership, World, release, and origin delivery; linked Web A and Telegram A share authorized continuity.
journeys.negativeProof: Telegram B cannot read A's receipts or workbench and never receives A's reply; webhook replay creates no second operation.
journeys.replayProof: The same signed webhook event resolves to one operation and one logical reply through its verified origin.
journeys.isolationProof: Telegram B remains a separate Account and World context and cannot read or receive data from A.
journeys.recoveryProof: A restart preserves channel bindings, the Membership workbench, and delivery state, then resumes only the verified origin.

participants.requiredBinding: Better Auth A to Account A to Membership A
participants.realAction: Start a conversation and commit a governed memory
participants.backendEvidence: `TurnCapability` records Account A, Membership A, active release, and operation
participants.visibleEvidence: The receipt appears in the same authenticated workbench

participants.requiredBinding: Telegram subject A to a verified binding chosen for fixture A
participants.realAction: Send nonce A from the visible Telegram A account
participants.backendEvidence: Audit records binding A, World A, operation A, and delivery A
participants.visibleEvidence: Reply appears only in Telegram A

participants.requiredBinding: Telegram subject B to Account B and Membership B
participants.realAction: Revalidate the visible account, then send nonce B
participants.backendEvidence: Audit records binding B, World B, operation B, and delivery B
participants.visibleEvidence: Reply appears only in Telegram B; nonce A and receipt A are absent

participants.realAction: Send a real message in the test thread
participants.backendEvidence: Signature, binding, operation, and delivery are recorded
participants.visibleEvidence: Reply appears in the same thread and not in either Telegram account

participants.requiredBinding: Existing delivery intents for A and B
participants.realAction: Restart after commit and around provider send
participants.backendEvidence: One logical operation and one stable delivery intent survive
participants.visibleEvidence: Each origin sees at most one logical reply

journeys.name: Durable automation
journeys.actors: Person asking Eve for two reminders
journeys.path: Generic Automation creates two ExecutorCall records; Restate survives restart, and each reminder reaches its verified origin once.
journeys.negativeProof: The kernel contains no Telegram, Kapso, WhatsApp, reminder Action ID, or provider branch; an ambiguous send reconciles without channel fallback.
journeys.replayProof: Restate retries the same ExecutorCall idempotency identity and creates no duplicate logical delivery.
journeys.isolationProof: Calls, credentials, payloads, and delivery origins remain scoped to their World and Membership.
journeys.recoveryProof: Application and Restate restarts resume pending attempts; an unknown send outcome is reconciled before another effect.

journeys.name: Agent parity
journeys.path: CLI, Connect, MCP, and Eve discover the same catalog and produce the same proposal, decision, receipt, and explanation.
journeys.negativeProof: A workload outside its Membership, release, or budget is denied by the same policy as a human.
journeys.replayProof: The same operation through any surface returns the original receipt and effect status without a new commit.
journeys.isolationProof: No surface bypasses Membership, release, or budget checks or crosses a World boundary.
journeys.recoveryProof: After reconnect or restart, every surface retains the operation basis and rediscovers the same active catalog.

journeys.name: Production recovery
journeys.path: The image boots from empty development state, reaches the projection watermark, registers ZoenEffect, passes product dependencies, restarts, and recovers.
journeys.negativeProof: Stopped projection, missing handler, stale release, broken Eve, or broken Better Auth makes /ready fail; authority remains immutable.
journeys.replayProof: Repeated boot, setup, and migrations converge without duplicate releases, receipts, or effects.
journeys.isolationProof: Least-privilege process credentials keep authority, projection, Eve, and effect access separated.
journeys.recoveryProof: A killed process or application restart returns /ready only after the watermark, handler, active release, Eve, and Better Auth recover.

finalGates.name: Ambiguous identity
finalGates.proof: IBM resolves to typed, contextual candidates without selecting the first ticker match.

finalGates.name: Competing provider evidence
finalGates.proof: An IBM KnowledgeBasisDefinition produces a durable ResolutionDecision while preserving visible rivals.

finalGates.name: Dense observation series
finalGates.proof: A year of IBM OHLCV becomes immutable segments and one accepted DatasetVersion boundary.

finalGates.name: SEC restatement
finalGates.proof: Two knowledge cuts return the IBM filing value known at each cut without deleting the original filing.

finalGates.name: Data entitlement
finalGates.proof: Every interface hides unauthorized IBM fields, series, counts, lineage, citations, and derived output before scanning.

finalGates.name: Derived adjusted series
finalGates.proof: An adjusted IBM series cites raw segments, event evidence, component digest, parameters, calendar, policy, and knowledge cut.

finalGates.name: Governed portfolio change
finalGates.proof: An IBM portfolio rebalance separates the authority Commit from the broker effect and reconciles an ambiguous result.

finalGates.name: Provider schema evolution
finalGates.proof: An IBM provider shape change activates one coherent four-catalog release and leaves the prior release queryable.

finalGates.name: Interface parity
finalGates.proof: Eve, CLI, Connect, and MCP resolve the same IBM type, Action, policy result, operation basis, and CommitReceipt.
